The security modules detect credential patterns and replace matches with `[REDACTED…]` markers before text is written out. The scanner replaces whole matches with `[REDACTED — <name> detected in <path>]`, and `redact.js` masks each pattern match as `[REDACTED:<name>]`. `patterns.js` holds the pattern list they use. `src/cache/entry.js` and `src/mcp/handlers.js` call the scanner, so cached entries and MCP tool output (such as `get_lines`) are redacted as well.

`src/security/scanner.js`

`src/retrieval/body-words.js`

SigMap scans extracted signatures against a bank of secret patterns and replaces any match with a `[REDACTED …]` marker before it reaches the generated context. `scanner.js` does the signature scanning, `patterns.js` holds the regexes, and `entry.js` applies the scan (gated by the `secretScan` setting) and fails closed. `redact.js` is the standalone text redactor that session and other output paths reuse. `body-words.js` filters secret-looking lines out of the indexed body words.

I located these by grepping for `secret` and `redact` and reading the matching lines, not by opening each file in full.
